`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Keeping one selected operation for the whole request is what makes "native" cheap. Rust and Go hold their selection state across every point they answer in one request, while each bounded query is still charged its own work. Python opened a fresh native request for each point, so moving its hooks onto native answers without fixing that first would have multiplied setup cost on every call.
- `BoundedResolution::Complete` doesn't mean "unique answer". It means "finished within budget". The value inside still carries a status such as `Resolved`, `Ambiguous` or `Incomplete`. That two-layer status is what lets the ruling's "typed open reason" survive all the way to the golden output, instead of being flattened into "not found".
